text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:

- State-owned companies this year plan to take about 188 billion tolars ($1.2 billion) of loans abroad and another 250 billion tolars at home, the Ministry of Finance said. Most loans will be spent for highway construction, export subsidies and investment in electricity and telecommunications infrastructure.

- Slovenia recently established ties with the government of the Serbian Republic in order to improve living conditions of some 500 Slovenians staying there and to start economic cooperation between the two countries.
- Christian Democrats said they would hold a congress in June when they would elect a new leadership in order to improve the standing of the party.

- Differences among social classes regarding access to educational and health institutions are widening in Slovenia, in line with similar changes in the rest of western and eastern Europe, sociologists said at an annual meeting in Portoroz.
- Slovenia's basketball team Smelt Olimpija will participate in the European Final Four basketball tour that starts in Rome on Tuesday.

- Slovenian diplomats will continue their extensive international activities this week to help the country be among the first that will extend NATO and the European Union. High-ranking officials will visit Brussels, Washington, Berlin and Geneva.
